scope: Additional quantitative archaeological and food-system evidence; out-of-period analogues remain validation-only.

promotion_audit.decision: These records add bounded quantitative tests but are not global scale anchors. The Maya record is out of period; Tiwanaku is a modeled agricultural potential without saturation evidence; Nukunonu is an ethnographic analogue. They must remain validation-only.

records.label: Classic Maya central lowlands, regional LiDAR settlement reconstruction
pressure_evidence: Estrada-Belli et al. (Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports, 2025) combine airborne LiDAR and archaeological settlement models over approximately 95,000 km2 in Peten, western Belize, Campeche and Quintana Roo; the revised regional estimate reaches about 16 million people at Late Classic peak.
The same study identifies repeated rural residential units, plazas and agricultural infrastructure across the surveyed landscape rather than treating a single city as the population boundary.

Johnston (Journal of Anthropological Archaeology 22, 2003, pp. 126-161) documents intensive dryfield cultivation and forest-fallow constraints as the lowland Maya food-production base, with density varying by local ecology.
records.trade_dependence: low_to_mixed; maize, beans, squash, manioc and managed forest foods were locally produced, while elite and inter-site exchange connected centers
records.boundary_description: The 95,000 km2 LiDAR and archaeological survey footprint spanning Guatemala's Peten, western Belize, Campeche and Quintana Roo; it is a regional rural-and-urban landscape, not the catchment of one city.
records.boundary_source: Estrada-Belli et al., New regional-scale Classic Maya population density estimates and settlement distribution models through airborne lidar scanning (Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports, 2025), study-area map and methods; Oxford Handbook of Historical Ecology and Applied Archaeology chapter by Isendahl/Smith (2013).
records.source_family_independence: LiDAR settlement reconstruction and independent agricultural-land-use synthesis are treated as one regional Maya source family; this group is held out because the dates precede the 1337 target.
records.notes: The population interval is a published LiDAR-based regional reconstruction, not a saturated equilibrium. The available EU5 Peten and Mayaab tags cover only about 86% of the published study footprint by calibrated area; the remainder is explicitly unmapped rather than silently filled. Keep entirely validation-only and never use the estimate as a 1337 target.

records.label: Tiwanaku three-valley raised-field sustaining area
pressure_evidence: Kolata, The Technology and Organization of Agricultural Production in the Tiwanaku State, Latin American Antiquity 2(2), 1991, pp. 109-112, maps approximately 19,000 ha of fossil raised fields in the Tiwanaku Valley, Pampa Koani and Machaca/Desaguadero and reports experimental potato yields.

Kolata Table 6, p. 112, gives 285,000-555,750 people for one crop with 75% field utilization and 570,000-1,111,500 for double cropping with 75% utilization; Table 5 gives the corresponding 100%-utilization bounds.
Kolata pp. 112-113 explicitly treats these as agricultural potential and states that estimated Tiwanaku population did not exhaust the ceiling; this is why the record is not a saturation target.

Erickson, Raised Fields as Monumental Farmed Landscapes, Sourcebook for Garden Archaeology (2013), pp. 724-728, documents mapped field extent, frost mitigation, canal fertility, experiments and a conservative estimate of one hectare supporting about 30 people for a year.
records.trade_dependence: low for staple calories; raised-field potatoes, highland tubers, camelid herding and lake fisheries were local, with exchange of non-staples
records.boundary_description: The three-valley Tiwanaku sustaining area (Tiwanaku Valley, Pampa Koani and Machaca/Desaguadero) containing approximately 19,000 ha of documented raised fields, as mapped in Kolata Figure 1 and Tables 5-6.
records.boundary_source: Kolata 1991, Figure 1 and Tables 5-6, pp. 103-113; Erickson 2013, pp. 724-728.
records.source_family_independence: Experimental raised-field production and archaeological mapping from the Tiwanaku sustaining area are one source family; no observed population is converted into a target.
records.notes: This is a technology-compatible physical-capacity validation envelope, not evidence that the region was at the Malthusian ceiling. Its explicit bounds test whether the mechanistic model can represent frost-buffered raised fields, rotations and high-altitude local food without importing starting population or historical cropland shares.

records.label: Nukunonu/Tokelau atoll local-food demographic analogue
pressure_evidence: Bayliss-Smith's Tokelau atoll study, as reproduced in Sear et al. Journal of Pacific Archaeology 16(2), 2026, Table A1 (p. 30), gives 1,640 people for Tokelau on 10.1 km2 (162 people/km2) using demographic reconstruction.

The source treats small atolls as drought-sensitive systems whose food supply depends on coconut, pulaka/taro pits, breadfruit, reef and lagoon fisheries, with severe freshwater and storm constraints.
The observed interval is an analogue for a hostile, resource-bounded island and not a 1337 census or saturation estimate.
records.trade_dependence: mixed; local staples and fishing dominate subsistence but modern transport and imported foods affect the observation
records.boundary_description: Nukunonu island/atoll in Tokelau; the EU5 geometry has one Nukunonu atoll location tag, but its calibrated game footprint is coarser than the 10.1 km2 land area in Bayliss-Smith's demographic table.
records.boundary_source: Sear et al. 2026, Table A1, p. 30, reproducing Bayliss-Smith's Tokelau demographic reconstruction; island area and food-system caveats are retained.
records.source_family_independence: Ethnographic/demographic atoll reconstruction; retained only as an out-of-period hostile-island analogue.
records.notes: Use only to test whether the model produces sensible uncertainty and low absolute capacity for freshwater-limited atolls. Do not train, scale or treat modern trade-supported population as a 1337 equilibrium.
